about: Hand-written approved summaries for the context experiment's brief (DECISIONS.md D84). bob's paused lockout attempt holds the trap's reason; alice, chen and dana add unrelated but plausible items on other files under src/auth and on src as a whole.

summaries.whatWasDone: Replaced plain SHA-256 password hashes with scrypt and a random 16-byte salt per user, stored as salt:hash, and compared with a timing-safe check.

decisions.decision: Passwords are hashed with scrypt and a random 16-byte salt per user.
decisions.reason: SHA-256 is too fast to slow down guessing if the user table leaks.

rejectedApproaches.approach: Using the native bcrypt module for hashing.
rejectedApproaches.reason: It needs a compiler at install time and the build failed on the slim production image.

summaries.goal: Lock accounts after repeated failed logins.
summaries.whatWasDone: Started an account lockout in the login handler, then paused the ticket for the billing release before it was finished.

rejectedApproaches.approach: Counting failed logins per account in the in-process cache in src/lib/cache.js.
rejectedApproaches.reason: Production runs three instances behind the load balancer and redeploys several times a day, so each instance keeps its own count and every deploy resets it, which gives an attacker far more than 5 tries.

risksOrFollowUps: Finish the lockout after the billing release.

summaries.whatWasDone: Login now creates a session token of 32 random bytes, stored in the shared key-value store under session:<token> for 24 hours.

decisions.decision: Session tokens are 32 random bytes kept in the key-value store for 24 hours.
decisions.reason: A server-side session can be ended at once on logout or when an account is compromised.

rejectedApproaches.approach: Signed JWT sessions with no server-side state.
rejectedApproaches.reason: A JWT can't be revoked before it expires, so logging out or blocking a stolen session wouldn't work.

summaries.whatWasDone: Every handler under src now returns an { ok, reason } object instead of throwing for expected failures. Emails are trimmed and lower-cased before lookup, and log lines no longer include email addresses.

decisions.decision: Handlers return { ok, reason } objects for expected failures instead of throwing.
decisions.reason: Callers branch on the reason code, and thrown errors were turning into 500 responses.

decisions.decision: Email addresses are trimmed and lower-cased before a user lookup.
decisions.reason: Users typed their email with capitals or a trailing space and were told the account didn't exist.

decisions.decision: Log lines never include email addresses.
decisions.reason: The logs go to a third-party service that isn't covered by the privacy policy.
